meta.title: MapleStory class roster and class guides
meta.worldAssumption: Heroic (Reboot) unless a record says otherwise
meta.verificationPolicy: Same three computed states as data/guide-graph.json — VERIFIED (source is a URL, a human opened it on lastVerified), UNVERIFIED (source starts with 'UNVERIFIED — ' and lastVerified is empty), STALE (patchVersion is behind meta.gameVersion) — PLUS a third axis this file adds: claimType is 'fact' (falsifiable in-game in seconds), 'consensus' (several independent guides agree, no primary source) or 'judgement' (this guide's own call). A class guide is mostly judgement by volume, and without the third state the whole feature renders as a wall of UNVERIFIED and nobody reads it.
meta.stalenessNote: Every roster figure is stamped v.269 because the best GMS-specific source (Grandis Library) is footer-stamped GMS Ver. 269 and the MapleStory Wiki is region-agnostic and not version-stamped at all. They are therefore STALE against the app's declared v.271 by construction, not by neglect. The v.270 and v.271 class deltas could not be read: the Nexon patch-notes page is a JS SPA that returns no text to a fetcher and docs/sources/v271-patch-notes.md is not present in this repo.

licensing.icons: NO GAME ART SHIPS IN THIS APP. Nexon's Game IP Guide for Content Creators states 'Commercial use of UGC is prohibited' and 'You may not sell, display, or otherwise provide access to UGC in return for monetary compensation'; its only monetisation carve-out is ads or donations on platforms anyone can access free, which a subscription app is not. That binds regardless of where the file came from, so hotlinking a community CDN does not cure it — and maplestorywiki.net is separately CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, which a paid tier contradicts on its own. Class marks in this file are therefore typographic: a monogram plus a branch colour, rendered from tokens, with zero external image dependency.
licensing.text: Class names, skill names, skill IDs and job-advancement order are facts and short phrases, not protectable expression, and nominative fair use covers naming them. In-game skill DESCRIPTION prose is not: the wiki's text is CC BY-NC-SA over Nexon's own wording, so every description in this file is written here rather than paraphrased from it.
licensing.pictograms: If a pictogram is ever wanted, game-icons.net is CC BY 3.0 with commercial use permitted on attribution ('Icons made by {author}. Available on https://game-icons.net') and is third-party fantasy art with no Nexon interest attached.

integration.damage: lib/damage.ts is the authority on damage constants. Guide records reference BOW_MASTER by path (the `from` field on a skill effect) and never restate a value.
integration.legion: lib/legion.ts owns the rank and link-level ladders. lib/classes.ts imports LINK_EFFECT and cross-checks it against this roster instead of forking it; see legionCrossCheck().
integration.guideGraph: data/guide-graph.json#nodes.v and #nodes.hexa hold the class-agnostic explainer. Keep them as the explanation of what a boost node IS and let the per-class plans own the ordering, or the two will contradict each other within one patch cycle.

bowmaster.summary: A DEX bowman built around one long keydown line, three stacking Final Damage buffs and a large native crit block. Its distinguishing planning property is that most of the numbers a damage calculator wants are ALREADY in the stat window: 75% crit rate, 31% crit damage, 20% boss damage and 57.25% stacked IED arrive from passives, so a Bow Master reaches the crit cap and approaches the IED wall earlier than almost any other class, and the usual 'more crit, more IED' advice stops paying long before the character feels finished. That is what this guide is for: naming the point where each line goes dead for THIS character rather than in general.

conditionalRules.rationale: Critical Rate above 100% does nothing. Bow Master carries 75% before hyper stats, Legion, links or gear (BOW_MASTER.alreadyInStatWindow.critRate), which is why this line goes dead earlier here than on almost any other class. The reference character sits at 98% printed: two points of headroom, then every further point is waste.

Below the IED wall the defence term is zero or negative and the damage index means nothing — lib/damage.ts clamps it and warns. Above it, IED sources stack multiplicatively, so each further line buys fewer effective points; lib/damage.ts marginalIedLine() reports how many a specific cube line actually buys. Bow Master arrives with 57.25% stacked from passives, which is already most of the way to the ~66.7% wall on a 300% PDR boss.

Once crit rate is capped, crit damage is the line the crit points should move to. This is an ordering judgement, not a game fact; the app should confirm it by comparing marginal() rows for critRate and critDmg on the loaded character rather than trusting the sentence.
conditionalRules.source: UNVERIFIED — ordering judgement. It is computable per character with lib/damage.ts marginal(), which is the honest way to settle it

innerAbility.stopRule: Stop when slot 1 is a Legendary Boss Damage +20% (or a crit rate line while you are genuinely short of the cap) and the other two slots are not actively harmful. Inner ability is the largest open-ended meso sink available mid-game, and the only advice that saves money is the instruction to stop. Rerolling a good slot-1 line to chase a perfect slot-2 is how accounts lose a week of income.

bands.focus: Hyper Skill passives arrive at 140, 150, 165, 180 and 190.

bands.gate: Lv 200 — 5th job and the V matrix.

bands.focus: 5th job. Slots are the constraint, not nodes.
bands.whatStartsMattering: Finishing ONE boost node rather than levelling several. Boost nodes are final damage and a Lv 1 node is nearly nothing.
bands.whatToStopDoing: Hoarding nodestones for a perfect trio while running an empty matrix.

bands.focus: Link skills hit level 3 at 210; the V matrix fills out.
bands.whatStartsMattering: Every mule at 210 rather than 200 — that is the second half of the account's link value.
bands.whatToStopDoing: Buying crit rate anywhere once the stat window is at the cap.

bands.focus: Slots stop being the constraint; Sol Erda Fragments become it.
bands.whatStartsMattering: Banking Sol Erda Fragments on the character that will reach 260 first — they are permanent and untradable, so the banking starts BEFORE they can be spent, sixteen-plus levels early.
bands.whatToStopDoing: Waiting until 260 to think about fragments.

bands.whatStartsMattering: Mastery node first, then boosts; the 10/20/30 breakpoints over a flat push to 30.
bands.whatToStopDoing: Spreading Sol Erda across nodes evenly.
